question: Why does a kitchen keep the most-used ingredients on a counter next to the stove?
options: Because a counter lets the storeroom hand out more ingredients at once
Because most orders use the same few items, so a nearby copy saves many trips to the storeroom
Because food on the counter never needs checking
Because every order needs different ingredients
explanation: This is caching: a small, fast copy of the data that most requests need. It does not make the storeroom itself faster; it means fewer trips to it. It works because orders repeat, and it needs freshness rules, because the copy can go stale.
